title: Спасительный звонок от Лёвы  (The Lifesaving Call from Lyova)

segments.t: Just minutes into the park run, an out-of-shape Chef Barinov is gasping for air while trying desperately to hide his exhaustion from Elena. Fortunately, his pre-arranged phone call from Lyova rings right on cue, allowing Viktor Petrovich to pretend he is urgently needed back at the restaurant.
Лёва, я просил, не звонить мне, я занят.
Ну что, завтра здесь же, это же время.
Let's walk back through the scene line by line.
'Just a second, right now.' Jumping in promptly during the talk, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 3 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
'Right here.' Replying candidly to Lyova, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 2 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
'I am coming right now!' Lyova speaks up pointedly in their talk, watching Vika's face to see how the news lands.
Лёва, я просил, не звонить мне, я занят.
'Lyova, I asked you not to call me when I am busy.' Underscoring how busy he is with Lyova, Barinov brings in "zanyat" ("busy", from "zanyatyy") as the key Russian word here.
'All right, fine, I will be right there.' Reacting warmly on the spot, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 4 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
'Yes, they are urgently calling me in to work.' Vika jumps in quietly around Lyova, grounding the moment in plain reality.
'Are you really leaving already, huh?' Lyova fires back promptly in the exchange and chooses "ukhodite" ("leave, go away", from the root "ukhodit") so Vika hears the exact meaning.
'Well, it cannot be helped.' Weighing in readily around Lyova, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 2 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
'Oh, I envy your stamina.' Lyova proceeds decisively without a pause, so Vika knows he is not just making small talk.
Ну что, завтра здесь же, это же время.
'Well then, tomorrow at the same place, same time.' Highlighting the time beside Lyova, Vika reaches for the Russian word "vremya" ("time") right at the heart of the line.
'Yes, of course.' Leaning in quietly right here, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 4 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
'See you tomorrow, then.' Vika weighs in decisively around Lyova, shifting the mood of the conversation in a single beat.

'Thank you for the company.' Lyova quietly uses this word of thanks right on cue using "spasibo" ("thank you") — the everyday word for "thank you", which grew out of the old blessing "spasi Bog" ("God save you").
Лёва, я просил, не звонить мне, я занят.
Ну что, завтра здесь же, это же время.

That wraps up this scene as gasping for breath after barely jogging a few hundred meters, Chef Barinov has Lyova call his phone so he can pretend an urgent kitchen emergency requires him at work. Until next time!
